items.definition:
to relate or connect with one another
The different aspects of the problem interrelate in complex ways.

to speak or write about in an abusively disparaging manner
The media tried to vilify the politician during the scandal.

to set free
The new law will emancipate many people from debt.

to surprise someone greatly
His sudden resignation flabbergasted everyone in the office.

to speak about (someone) in a spitefully critical manner
He tried to malign his opponent's reputation.

to transfer from private to state ownership or control (British English)
The government decided to nationalise the struggling industry.

spread throughout (something); pervade
The smell of baking bread permeated the entire house.

make (someone) anxious or unsettled
The news of the accident did not seem to perturb him.

increase rapidly in numbers; multiply
Rumors about the incident began to proliferate.

seize and carry off (someone); fill (someone) with intense delight
The beauty of the landscape ravished his senses.

run with short, quick steps; sink (one's own ship)
The crab began to scuttle sideways into its hole.

bring under domination or control
The empire sought to subjugate the neighboring tribes.

not to deter or discourage
Nothing could undaunt his resolve.

support from below; form the basis of
The research underpins the new theory.

to become less intense or widespread
The storm finally began to abate.

dig out (something buried, especially a corpse) from the ground
The police decided to exhume the body for further examination.

erase or remove completely (something unwanted or unpleasant)
He tried to expunge the painful memories from his mind.

chop or cut (something, especially wood or coal) with an axe, pick, or other tool
The sculptor began to hew the stone into shape.

(Of a monarch) renounce one's throne.
The king decided to abdicate his throne.

to assert or confess openly
He avowed his innocence despite the evidence.

to remain or stay somewhere
He decided to bide his time until the right opportunity arose.

to free from illusion or false belief; disillusion
The harsh reality of the job began to disenchant him.

to isolate or hide away; to take legal possession of
The jury was sequestered during the trial.

to hold (someone's attention) completely as though by magic
The magician's performance spellbound the audience.

to argue or dispute; to herd animals
They spent hours trying to wrangle the cattle.

to spoil or make impure
They were accused of trying to defile the sacred monument.

to pretend to be affected by (a feeling, state, or injury)
She tried to feign illness to avoid going to school.

destroy (something, especially waste material) by burning
The old documents were incinerated to protect privacy.

criticize in an abusive or angrily insulting manner
He was reviled by the public for his controversial statements.

Reject with disdain or contempt.
She spurned his advances and walked away.

Include or absorb (something) in something else.
The new theory attempts to subsume all previous findings.

detest; strongly dislike
She truly abhors violence in any form.

form a concept or idea of (something); imagine
It's hard to conceptualize the vastness of space.

secretly allow (something immoral, illegal, or harmful) to occur
The guards were accused of conniving with the prisoners.

publicly denounce
The critics decried the new policy as unfair.

treat (a sacred place or thing) with violent disrespect; violate
Vandals desecrated the ancient monument.

to force out (a material) through a die or nozzle
Plastic is often extruded into various shapes.

to exhaust or wear out; to kill (an old or injured animal)
The long hike really knackered me out.

extend beyond limits
The government was accused of overreaching its authority.

imagine again or anew
The director decided to reimagine the classic play for a modern audience.

to be generally considered or believed to be
He is reputed to be the best doctor in the city.

to make something sexual in nature or character
The media often tends to sexualize female athletes.

To make less severe
He tried to assuage her fears about the upcoming exam.

to come together to form one mass or whole
The small groups will coalesce into one large organization.

To make a living with difficulty; to obtain or extract with great effort.
They had to eke out a living from their small farm.

To cause or give rise to (a feeling, situation, or condition).
The new policy is likely to engender controversy.

forcibly pull (something) from a person's grasp
He managed to wrest the document from her hand.

to consider or declare to be true or the case
The court will adjudge the winner of the competition.

to adjust a rate or amount to an annual basis
We need to annualize these quarterly earnings to get a full-year projection.

prevent or obstruct by taking action ahead of time
He tried to forestall the crisis by acting quickly.

to exclude from a society or group
The community decided to ostracize him after his controversial remarks.

to transfer (a business, industry, or service) from public to private ownership and control
The government plans to privatise several state-owned industries.

to make amends to (someone) for loss or harm suffered; compensate
The company offered to recompense customers for the inconvenience.

refuse to accept or be associated with; deny the truth or validity of
He was quick to repudiate the accusations made against him.

revive (someone) from unconsciousness or apparent death
Paramedics tried to resuscitate the victim at the scene.

sharpen the blade of (a tool or weapon); excite or stimulate (someone's desire, interest, or appetite)
The appetizer only served to whet my appetite.

to draw (fluid) by suction from a body cavity; to pronounce with an audible breath
The doctor had to aspirate fluid from the patient's lung.

To restrict (something) within limits; to draw a figure around another, touching it at points
The new rules will circumscribe the power of the committee.

to portray as evil or threatening
It's easy to demonize those we don't understand.

to do dull, laborious, or menial work
He had to drudge through piles of paperwork.

to discharge slowly and steadily; to display (an emotion or quality) strongly and openly
The plant began to exude a sticky sap.

compensate (someone) for harm or loss; secure (someone) against legal responsibility for their actions
The insurance policy will indemnify you against any losses.

to process substances in the body
The body metabolizes food to produce energy.

to adapt for use as a weapon
The country was accused of trying to weaponize the virus.
